title: CHAPTER 12: BANKING TECHNOLOGY AND IT IN BANKING

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Core Banking System (CBS) centralizes database processing, enabling seamless 'Anywhere Banking' across all branch networks.
Payment infrastructure in India is managed by RBI (RTGS, NEFT) and NPCI (UPI, IMPS, NETC FASTag, AePS).
Open Banking utilizes secure Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) to permit controlled data sharing with fintech partners.
Bank IT infrastructure requires high availability through Primary Data Centers (DC) backed by geographically isolated Disaster Recovery (DR) sites.
RBI IT guidelines enforce strict Cyber Security Frameworks, regular Vulnerability Assessment & Penetration Testing (VAPT), and Security Operations Center (SOC) monitoring.

blocks.content: Core Banking Solution (CBS) is a centralised system that allows banking transactions to be processed across all branches of a bank in real-time. It replaces isolated branch-level systems with a unified, centralised database.

cells: All branches access same database; real-time updates; no end-of-day reconciliation between branches
Customer can transact from any branch or channel
Integrates ATM, mobile banking, internet banking, POS on single platform
Infosys Finacle, TCS BaNCS, Oracle FLEXCUBE, Temenos T24, Nucleus FinnOne
SBI migrated fully to TCS BaNCS; largest CBS migration in the world
All RRBs mandated to implement CBS by RBI; NABARD provided funding assistance

items: RTGS settles transactions continuously on an individual basis with a minimum threshold of ₹2 Lakhs, whereas NEFT settles in half-hourly net batches with no minimum limit.
NPCI (National Payments Corporation of India) was established in 2008 under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.
RBI guidelines require regulated entities to report any major cyber security incident to the RBI within 2 to 6 hours of detection.
